title: DPHGNN: A Dual Perspective Hypergraph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Changes in hypergraph topology can contribute to suboptimal performance in hypergraph neural networks.

gap.claim: Existing spatial and spectral hypergraph neural networks do not adequately capture lower-order semantics while handling hypergraph topology.

contributions.claim: DPHGNN is a dual-perspective hypergraph neural network that uses equivariant operator learning and dynamically fuses lower-order explicit feature representations from an underlying graph into a super-imposed hypergraph structure.

The work provides a theoretical framework and a synthetic hypergraph isomorphism test for expressing the power of spatial hypergraph neural networks and quantifying DPHGNN expressivity beyond the Generalized Weisfeiler Leman 1-GWL test.
DPHGNN was deployed for Return-to-Origin prediction by the partner e-commerce company Meesho.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DPHGNN as a novel dual-perspective hypergraph neural network.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On eight benchmark hypergraph datasets for semi-supervised hypernode classification, DPHGNN reportedly outperformed seven state-of-the-art baselines.
In the Meesho Return-to-Origin prediction deployment, DPHGNN reportedly achieved a macro F1-Score 7% higher than the best baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Message passing on hypergraphs is presented as a standard framework for learning higher-order correlations, with hypergraph neural networks categorized as spatial or spectral.
The authors analyze topology-related suboptimal performance and propose DPHGNN, which combines topology-aware spatial and spectral inductive biases with lower-order semantic information.
The method is benchmarked on eight hypergraph datasets for semi-supervised hypernode classification against seven baselines.
The work adds an expressivity analysis and synthetic isomorphism test, then reports deployment for Return-to-Origin prediction with a macro F1-Score improvement over the best baseline.

source_observation.claim: The method dynamically fuses lower-order explicit feature representations from an underlying graph with a hypergraph structure.

interpretation.claim: Combining representations of different structural orders may help address information loss or instability caused by relying on a single graph perspective.

application.claim: For higher-order relational learning, consider jointly modeling explicit lower-order structure and higher-order relations when both are available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when dual-perspective fusion is beneficial or what data conditions are required.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the mechanisms or settings by which hypergraph topology affects performance.
Dataset identities, splits, metrics beyond macro F1-Score, and experimental settings are omitted.
Theoretical assumptions, proof details, and the construction of the synthetic isomorphism test are omitted.
Deployment scale, operational conditions, and independent verification of the reported results are omitted.
